A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AQUA, with matching authors, core methods and original experiments. All 18 pages of v1 and 29 pages of v2, including figures, equations, tables and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original watermark detection experiments on MMQA and WebQA, including effectiveness, harmlessness, stealthiness and image-transformation results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and reports additional filtering, regeneration, fine-tuning, model-scale and deployment-drift results.

M1.justification: The core acronym/OCR and spatial watermark procedures remain. Appendix A.4 adds an explicitly optional caption pipeline combining low-co-occurrence concepts with perplexity filtering, and Appendix B.2 proposes a centralized trigger registry. These extend the framework; the PDFs do not establish that the retained experiments used these extensions.

E1.justification: MMQA and WebQA remain the primary datasets. v2 additionally uses COCO and Alpaca-GPT4 samples for adversarial fine-tuning and evaluates substantially broader environments: VLM filtering, image regeneration, refusal-trained generators and MMQA corpora expanded with WebQA distractors.

E2.justification: Naive and Opt. remain the evaluated watermarking baselines. Their participation is unchanged in Table 1 and the retained diagnostic plots; v2 also includes both in the added Z-test comparison in Table 9.

E3.justification: v2 adds 2B–38B generator configurations, batch and single-image filtering protocols, adversarial fine-tuning with a 2,000-question utility evaluation, and retriever replacement/fine-tuning. Its image-attack evaluation uses WAVES strength 1 with Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Rank/CGSR reporting, replacing the earlier specified transformation experiments and Rank/p-value reporting.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained PCA, relevant-query and watermark-count analyses, v2 adds adaptive filtering, regeneration and repeated-diffusion attacks, model-scale analysis, refusal and fine-tuning tests, retriever updates and corpus drift. The earlier four-generator transformation supplement is removed. These changes substantially broaden the robustness questions investigated.

E5.justification: v2 adds two-proportion Z-test results in Table 9 and system/dataset-specific reference means and variances in Table 8. It also reports five independent runs for the new basic filtering experiment and explains conservative reference-variance broadening. Both versions retain ten repetitions for the main effectiveness experiment; no increase there is established.

E6.justification: Table 1 is unchanged, but extensive new results cover filtering, model scales, attacks and deployment variations. Table 12 reports 100% acronym detection by stringent OCR filtering with 61.44–72.02% FPR. The new fine-tuning study reports utility falling from 27.25% to 24.90%. Acronym-replacement ranks change from 5.00 in v1 Table 7 to 10.00 in v2 Table 11; the old transformation p-values are removed.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1 newly states and argues statistical assumptions concerning unequal variances, normality and independence for the verification tests. This adds limited mathematical reasoning, without formal proofs. The numbered retrieval, verification, metric and optimization equations retain their substance apart from notation clarifications.

C1.justification: The first-framework claim, two complementary strategies and black-box copyright-tracing contribution remain. v2 explicitly extends the introduction’s robustness claim from common image transformations to regeneration attacks and broadens the stated experimental contribution beyond the original four named VLMs.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of filtering versus false-positive costs, watermark suppression versus utility loss, model scaling, deployment drift and provider collisions. It also explains dataset-specific reference calibration. Conversely, v1 Section 6’s explicit limitation about watermark quality increasing verification queries and its discussion of extensions beyond T2T are removed.

D1.justification: v2 adds filter prompts, caption templates, reference-calibration instructions, attack-training data composition and detailed LoRA/NEFTune hyperparameters in Table 13. It adds a supplemental-code availability statement while retaining the repository link. The original A40 GPU and CPU specifications disappear.

R1.justification: v2 adds supporting references for WAVES, LoRA, NEFTune, SigLIP, newer VLMs and Xu et al.’s watermark verification work, while pruning several text-only RAG and future-work citations. Its substantive positioning relative to WARD, RAG-WM, RAG© and DMI-RAG remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction and experimental prose are extensively rewritten, including correction of 'exact match' to 'substring match.' The standalone Discussion is removed, deployment material moves into an expanded appendix, and supplementary experiments are reorganized. Ethics, reproducibility and LLM-use statements are added.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different conference layout, reformats tables and prompt boxes, merges v1 Figures 4–5 into v2 Figure 4, and relocates the unchanged watermark-count plot to the appendix. It adds numerous experimental tables and a 30-image gallery, and replaces several acronym examples with natural-scene variants.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evaluation of the central security claims: v1 relied largely on PCA and simple transformations, whereas v2 measures adaptive filtering, regeneration, fine-tuning and deployment drift, including effects on benign data and QA utility. Added implementation details and the corrected rank inconsistency improve auditability. These gains outweigh the loss of the explicit limitations discussion and earlier cross-generator transformation results, although the added arguments that repetitions and retrieval separation establish statistical assumptions remain insufficiently justified.
